visual: Compact, densely branched dwarf deciduous shrub with small rounded purplish-red to deep burgundy leaves, becoming brighter crimson-red in autumn; small pale yellow spring flowers are followed by glossy red berries.
water: Water regularly while establishing; mature plants tolerate moderately dry conditions.
aspect: South, east, west or north-facing; full sun to partial shade.
soil: Moist but well-drained or well-drained chalk, clay, loam or sandy soil; tolerant of acid, neutral and alkaline conditions.
soilWarning: Avoid persistently waterlogged ground; strongest purple-red foliage colour develops in good light.
prune: Little pruning required; remove damaged or unwanted stems after flowering and trim low hedges as necessary.
toxicity: Fruit is ornamental and should not be eaten; thorny stems can cause injury and gloves are recommended when handling.
resilience: Exceptionally cold hardy and tolerant of exposure, varied soils and periods of dryness once established.
uses: Low hedging, border edging, containers, rock gardens, colour contrast and low-maintenance shrub planting.

visual: Slow-growing evergreen shrub or small tree with glossy finely serrated dark green leaves and autumn to winter flowers ranging from white and pale pink to deep rose-pink; many cultivated forms are lightly fragrant.
water: Keep evenly moist, particularly during summer when the following season's flower buds are forming; rainwater is preferable in hard-water areas.
aspect: South, east, west or sheltered north-facing; sun to partial shade, with established plants tolerating more sun than many other camellias.
soil: Humus-rich, moist but well-drained acidic soil, ideally around pH 5.5–6.5.
soilWarning: Avoid alkaline or chalky soil, prolonged drought and cold exposed winds which can damage buds and flowers.
prune: Requires little pruning; lightly shape after flowering where necessary.
resilience: Hardy through much of the UK in a sheltered position, though flowers and buds can be damaged by severe frost and cold winds.
uses: Autumn colour, woodland gardens, sheltered borders, containers, courtyards and wall-side planting.
uncertain: The label phrases 'Les Camélias d’Automne' and 'floraison automne' describe autumn-flowering Camellia sasanqua rather than identifying a specific cultivar.

visual: Compact deciduous shrub with glossy green foliage and unusual spherical creamy-white flower heads covered in long projecting styles, creating a distinctive fibre-optic or pincushion appearance.
water: Keep consistently moist; particularly well suited to damp ground and can tolerate periodically wet conditions.
aspect: South, east or west-facing; full sun to partial shade.
soil: Humus-rich, moisture-retentive soil; performs especially well in consistently damp locations.
soilWarning: Avoid very dry sites where the root zone repeatedly dries out.
prune: Prune or lightly reshape in late winter or early spring before new growth begins.
resilience: Cold hardy and unusually tolerant of wet or periodically waterlogged soil once established.
uses: Rain gardens, pond margins, damp borders, wildlife gardens and pollinator planting.

visual: Compact spreading deciduous shrub with slender lance-shaped green leaves that develop vivid red autumn colour, contrasting with clusters of intensely rich blue plumbago-like flowers in late summer and autumn.
water: Water regularly while establishing; thereafter keep moderately moist but well drained.
aspect: South, east or west-facing; full sun to partial shade.
soil: Moist but well-drained or well-drained chalk, clay, loam or sandy soil; tolerant of acid, neutral and alkaline pH.
soilWarning: Avoid prolonged waterlogging; flowering and autumn foliage colour are strongest with good light.
prune: Prune in spring, cutting back old flowering growth to encourage vigorous new shoots.
resilience: Hardy through most of the UK and tolerant of exposed conditions provided the soil drains adequately.
uses: Border fronts, cottage gardens, gravel gardens, containers, wall-side planting and late-season colour.

visual: Dense bushy evergreen shrub with leathery dark green oval leaves and flattened clusters of deep pink flower buds opening to small starry white flowers from winter into spring, followed by metallic blue-black berries.
water: Water regularly during establishment; mature shrubs tolerate moderate dry periods but perform best with reliable moisture.
aspect: South, east, west or north-facing; full sun, partial shade or full shade.
soil: Moderately fertile, humus-rich, moist but well-drained or well-drained soil; tolerant of chalk, clay, loam and sand and most pH levels.
soilWarning: Avoid severe waterlogging and very exposed positions with persistent cold drying winds.
prune: Little routine pruning required; remove damaged or badly placed stems after flowering and trim hedges in spring.
toxicity: Fruit is ornamental and should not be eaten; gloves are advisable when handling.
resilience: Tough evergreen shrub tolerant of sun, shade, coastal exposure and a broad range of soils, though severe cold can damage young growth.
uses: Evergreen hedging, screening, shrub borders, wildlife gardens, coastal planting and winter-flowering displays.
